scheme_name: Large Sized Multi-Purpose Coop. Society: Medium Term Loan to Tribal Members
description:
The Large Sized Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to support tribal members through financial assistance. 

This scheme was introduced in the year 2008 as part of the broader strategy to empower tribal communities and enhance their socio-economic status. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide medium-term loans to tribal members for various income-generating activities. 

The scheme aims to uplift the living standards of tribal populations by facilitating access to credit. 

The target beneficiaries of this scheme are primarily tribal members who are part of large-sized multi-purpose cooperative societies. 

These societies play a crucial role in the economic development of tribal areas by providing various services including credit, marketing, and supply of inputs. 

The scheme is designed to provide loans ranging from INR 1 lakh to INR 10 lakh. 

The loan amount is determined based on the specific needs of the tribal members and the viability of the proposed project. 

The interest rate on these loans is set at a subsidized rate of 7 percent per annum. 

This interest rate is significantly lower than the prevailing market rates, making it easier for tribal members to repay the loans. 

The repayment period for the loans can extend up to 5 years. 

This allows beneficiaries ample time to generate income from their projects and repay the loans without financial strain. 

The scheme also aims to promote self-employment among tribal members. 

By providing financial assistance, the government encourages tribal members to start their own businesses or engage in agricultural activities. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a member of a large-sized multi-purpose cooperative society. 

Applicants must also belong to a Scheduled Tribe as defined by the Government of India. 

There is no specific age limit mentioned for eligibility. 

However, applicants must demonstrate a viable business plan or project proposal to qualify for the loan. 

The application process involves several steps to ensure that the funds are allocated to deserving candidates. 

First, eligible tribal members must approach their respective cooperative societies to express their interest in availing the loan. 

The cooperative society will then assist the members in preparing a detailed project report. 

This report must outline the proposed business or activity, expected costs, and projected income. 

Once the project report is prepared, it must be submitted to the cooperative society for approval. 

The society will review the proposal and assess its feasibility. 

If approved, the society will forward the application to the concerned district-level authority for final approval. 

The required documents for the application include proof of identity, proof of tribal status, and a detailed project report. 

Additionally, applicants may need to provide financial statements or income proof to demonstrate their ability to repay the loan. 

The timeline for processing the loan application can vary. 

Typically, it may take anywhere from 30 to 60 days for the entire process from application submission to loan disbursement. 

The disbursement of the loan is usually made in a single installment. 

However, in some cases, it may be disbursed in phases depending on the nature of the project. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India. 

The Ministry works in collaboration with state governments and cooperative societies to ensure effective implementation. 

Each state has its own designated department for tribal welfare that oversees the scheme at the state level. 

Contact details for the Ministry of Tribal Affairs can be found on their official website. 

The scheme has been instrumental in improving the economic conditions of tribal communities across India. 

According to reports, over 1 lakh tribal members have benefited from this scheme since its inception. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2023-24. 

This funding is aimed at expanding the reach of the scheme and increasing the number of beneficiaries. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of financial literacy among tribal members. 

Workshops and training sessions are conducted to educate beneficiaries about managing finances and repaying loans. 

The success of the scheme is measured through various indicators such as the number of loans disbursed and the repayment rate. 

As of 2023, the repayment rate for loans under this scheme stands at approximately 85 percent. 

This high repayment rate indicates the effectiveness of the scheme in promoting responsible borrowing and financial management. 

The government continuously monitors the implementation of the scheme to ensure transparency and accountability. 

Regular audits are conducted to assess the utilization of funds and the impact on beneficiaries. 

Feedback from tribal members is also collected to make necessary adjustments to the scheme. 

The scheme aligns with the broader goals of the Government of India to promote inclusive growth and reduce poverty among marginalized communities. 

It is part of the National Tribal Policy which aims to ensure the socio-economic development of tribal populations. 

Overall, the Large Sized Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society scheme is a vital initiative that empowers tribal members through financial support. 

By providing access to credit at subsidized rates, the scheme fosters entrepreneurship and self-reliance among tribal communities. 

The government remains committed to enhancing the welfare of tribal populations through such targeted interventions. 

This scheme is a testament to the government's efforts to bridge the economic gap and promote sustainable development in tribal areas. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a more equitable society where tribal members can thrive economically and socially. 

The scheme has the potential to transform the lives of many tribal families by providing them with the necessary resources to improve their livelihoods. 

In conclusion, the Large Sized Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society scheme is a comprehensive welfare initiative that addresses the financial needs of tribal members. 

It is an essential tool for promoting economic development and self-sufficiency among one of India's most vulnerable populations.
